title: Why you should stop playing videogames
summary: A two-hour testimony from NH as a former gaming addict, arguing that video games act as a consequence-free stand-in for real accomplishment that keeps young men stuck as boys, lowers standards, and is physically catabolic. He ranks the five worst game types (shooters, MMORPGs, MOBAs, sandbox, sports sims) and five least harmful ones (finite offline RPGs, RTS, platformers, puzzlers, party games), and says the cure is to swap the addiction for training.
claims: NH logged thousands of real hours on video games, quit around age 18-19 and had not played in about 8-9 years at the time of filming
Because he has an addictive personality he cannot moderate; he has to quit something completely or not at all
Escapism is fine as a short break before you face the problem, but if you never face it the break stops being recovery and becomes cowardice

Video games copy the reward mechanics of real achievement without the consequences, so they scratch the itch to achieve and remove the drive to do it in real life, much like porn tricks the brain into thinking it reproduced
Games are built around male instincts such as gaining status, gathering resources and saving someone, which is why the industry targets men
Games have been made easier since the 1990s to match players who avoid difficulty, and that casualisation lowers players' standards and breeds mediocrity
Every year he spent gaming as a teenager was a year he had to make up in his early 20s, socially and in personal development
Gaming is catabolic: hours of sitting still shrink muscle, and he expects heavy gamers would show lower muscle mass if studied
As a middle-schooler on holidays he gamed from 8 am to 8 pm, spent an hour with his mother, then played until midnight, about 12-14 hours a day
Gamers either forget to eat and drink or snack on soda and chips; bad habits come in pairs and gaming ends up costing sleep, diet, social life and training sessions
Without quitting games he believes he would be either overweight or very skinny and the channel would not exist
Screens and fast, flashy games given to young children damage their attention and likely contribute to the rise in ADHD; children should not game until they are mature enough
Online gaming friendships and Twitch communities feel social but leave you alone and socially unpractised, a pattern he calls the Twitch paradox
To earn a living from streaming you would need to be roughly in the top thousand streamers of your country, so gaming hours will almost never pay off
Shooters drain aggression that could be put to good use, raise anxiety and attention problems with nonstop fast pace, and respawning teaches that actions have no consequences
MMORPGs are endless, deliberately designed time sinks; he knows someone who put 10,000 hours into World of Warcraft
MOBAs, League of Legends especially, are the worst: you are one fifth of a random team, so outcomes feel out of your control, which breeds frustration, toxicity and refusal of responsibility
He says League matchmaking deliberately creates alternating wins and losses because frustration keeps people playing, the way a casino lets you win just enough
NH reached Diamond in League within his first year and played alongside semi-professional teams; he quit because the game made him depressed
Sandbox games such as Minecraft and The Sims offer god-like power with fake creativity, and sports simulations replace real physical activity with watching others play

Least harmful games are finite and can be paused: offline RPGs like Dark Souls, which tire you out after about 2 hours; RTS games, where you can only blame yourself; platformers; puzzlers; and party games played with real people
The more time a game demands, the worse it is for you; finite games beat endless ones
Cap gaming at roughly an hour a day and maybe two hours on weekend days, and never spend more hours per week gaming than training
The cure for gaming addiction is to move the addiction to lifting: training limits itself naturally, and afterwards an hour of gaming can work as recovery instead of replacing life
